# Thane & Reeve

> Thane & Reeve is a Boston-based, Northeast real estate firm that acquires, develops, and manages institutional-quality property under one accountable roof. It is organized around a single principle: the refusal to separate ownership from operations. The firm operates three divisions — Capital, Development, and Management — on one balance sheet, and invests meaningful personal (GP) capital in every transaction. Tagline: "Land held. Land managed."

## Key facts

- Legal entity: Thane & Reeve Holdings LLC
- Founded: 2026, by Patrick Barrett (Founder & Managing Partner) and Timothy Johnson (Co-Founder & Partner)
- Headquarters: Boston, Massachusetts
- Area served: the Boston–NYC corridor and the wider Northeast United States
- Capital raised/deployed: ~$82.75M across one ground-up development, one preservation project, and a ~75-door stabilized operating base (192 doors total referenced across the portfolio)
- Model: deal-by-deal syndication (LP/GP), no blind pools, no cross-collateralization; the GP commits personal capital to every deal
- Contact: contact@thaneandreeve.com · acquisitions@thaneandreeve.com (property submissions, read only by the partners)

## What the three divisions do

- **Capital** — sources, underwrites, structures, and syndicates real estate investments alongside family offices, high-net-worth principals, and institutional capital. Deal-by-deal, not a blind pool.
- **Development** — ground-up and entitlement-first development in submarkets where the firm has an information advantage. Builds what it intends to hold.
- **Management** — runs everything the firm owns in-house: asset management, property operations, leasing strategy, capital planning, and investor reporting. The firm's thesis is that most real-estate underperformance is operational, not strategic.

## Notable assets

- **907 Main — The Lark Cambridge**: a 67-key ground-up boutique hotel in Central Square, Cambridge, MA. ~$45M ground-up, ~$37.75M institutional financing, designed by Gensler Boston, opened 2024; owned and operated by the firm.
- **17 Story Street — Harriet Jacobs House**: historic preservation of a significant African American heritage site in Harvard Square, Cambridge, paired with new residential construction (50+ homes). Approved 7–0 by the Cambridge Historical Commission after five years of community work.

- Sitemap: https://thaneandreeve.com/sitemap.xml
- The firm is deliberately small and selective: "We will be small. We will be slow. We will walk from deals other firms will do."
